originality.rationale: Comparison by implication: Kosche et al. (arXiv:2108.13968, Section 3, Proposition 3.6) discuss the same periodic family but prove only an exponential lower bound for fixed even alphabets of size at least four; their argument expressly assumes sigma>=4. The new exact binary minimum-alphabet all-length MAS spectrum, local weak-descent characterization and growth constant are not obtained by that result. Adamson et al. 2024 treat counts of all absent (not necessarily minimal absent) words in a fixed length, and Manea et al. 2025 treat general enumeration algorithms. Targeted published-literature comparisons found no equivalent, including the nearest SAS extremal and universality-index results. Unindexed equivalents remain possible.

The exact integer sequence may appear in OEIS or other enumeration tables under different combinatorial interpretations; the OEIS targeted endpoint was not accessible.
The later primary papers were inspected for relevant scope and contributions but not all pages and appendices; a hidden relevant observation remains possible.

value.rationale: Kosche et al. establish exponential MAS growth for this periodic family only at even alphabet sizes >=4 and polynomial SAS counts. The exact binary MAS antichain spectrum fills a naturally motivated smallest-alphabet gap, gives a structural forbidden-pattern classification and sharp growth rate, and quantifies output size for canonical MAS enumeration instances. It is neither a textbook renaming nor a table recomputation.
